oil.summary: Crude markets posted modest gains on the day — Brent holding firmly near $100.72 (+0.40%) and WTI edging to $89.59 (+0.18%) — as the Gulf export recovery narrative wrestled with a complex geopolitical backdrop. Persian Gulf flows have recovered to 81% of pre-war levels, and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has moved 5.8 million barrels as the Red Sea route stabilises, though record freight costs and tanker-risk premiums are absorbing part of the supply benefit. The U.S. blockade has stranded at least 50 Iranian tankers, keeping Iranian barrels off market. Sanctions policy is bifurcated: President Trump signed new Russia-Iran sanctions legislation, yet separately the U.S. reportedly eased some Russia oil sanctions to cap price surges, angering European allies. Ukraine's strikes on Russian refining capacity — said to have crippled over half — provide an additional supply-side overhang. RBOB gasoline cratered 4.81% on the session, a notable divergence from crude.
drivers: Gulf export recovery (81% of pre-war levels) and Saudi East-West pipeline throughput cap the upside on crude, while record freight costs erode the supply benefit
Contradictory U.S. sanctions posture — new Russia/Iran sanctions law signed alongside temporary Russia sanction relief — creates headline volatility and policy uncertainty
RBOB gasoline down 4.81% on the day, diverging sharply from flat crude, likely reflecting demand or crack-spread normalization

gas.summary: Natural gas prices strengthened materially on both sides of the Atlantic. Henry Hub gained 1.60% to $3.115/MMBtu, extending a 4.71% monthly advance, while TTF surged 2.68% to €75.485/MWh — up more than 8% on the week and nearly 5% on the month. European price pressure is being exacerbated by geopolitical supply-route anxiety linked to Gulf corridor disruptions; Gulf producers called today for importers to share the cost of Hormuz bypass infrastructure, signalling that workaround costs will be passed downstream. The EU offered some relief on the regulatory front, granting exporters an extra year to comply with incoming methane rules to avoid layering further cost onto already-strained supply chains. News flow specific to gas fundamentals — storage, LNG flows, demand data — was limited in today's feed.
drivers: TTF surging 8%+ on the week as Gulf supply-route disruptions and Hormuz bypass cost-sharing demands elevate European gas risk premiums
EU delays methane regulations by one year, a modest regulatory relief measure aimed at keeping supply costs from rising further
Henry Hub trending higher (+4.71% monthly) in sympathy with global tightness, though domestic fundamental detail was thin in today's data

power.summary: The EU carbon EUA edged up 0.54% to $80.66, consolidating near recent levels despite a slight weekly pullback of 1.55%, with TTF's renewed surge providing underlying cost-side support for power generators. The dominant headline in European power today was the UK's second system margin warning in two weeks, issued by the National Energy System Operator due to low wind generation — a recurring vulnerability heading into autumn. A developing Gulf storm system was flagged as a potential threat to 3 million bpd of refining capacity, though the Atlantic hurricane season has so far been quiet under El Niño influence. Japan's engagement with Saudi Arabia and UAE at the AZEC meeting, focused on building reserve buffers, underscores persistent Asia-Pacific energy security anxiety that feeds into global power-sector cost assumptions.
drivers: UK grid under pressure for second time in two weeks as low wind output triggers National Energy System Operator margin warning
TTF at €75.49/MWh (+2.68% day) raises gas-fired generation costs and provides upward pressure on carbon allowance pricing
Gulf storm threat to 3 million bpd of refining capacity noted, though Atlantic season remains subdued under El Niño wind shear
